ecosystem.notes: Gross Bookings include Freight revenue, which Uber books gross, as well as taxes, tolls and fees. They exclude tips. Revenue includes Freight revenue. The 10-K does not state total driver or courier earnings, so payouts is null. 'Platform Participant direct transaction costs' (costs paid to Platform Earners that Uber records in cost of revenue, plus end-user incentives) are a partial, mixed amount, not total earnings, and are not used.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Uber presents revenue on a gross basis in markets where it is responsible for the Mobility, Delivery or Freight service, with payments to drivers and carriers in cost of revenue, so revenue ÷ Gross Bookings overstates what Uber keeps.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0001543151-26-000015). Marketplace: salesEnabled = Gross Bookings − revenue. In gross (principal) markets and Freight the fare is in both Gross Bookings and revenue and nets to zero, and driver pay is counted once, through paidOut; in agent markets driver earnings sit outside revenue and are counted once, through salesEnabled. Gross Bookings include taxes, tolls and fees and are before consumer discounts (overstates). Interest and income taxes paid are inside operating cash flow (US GAAP); the 10-K still prints both in the supplemental cash-flow disclosures, and the income-tax note gives the same 345 total by jurisdiction (US federal 12, US state and local 81, foreign 252).
